The Al-Ahsa Public Prosecution charged Sivarasa with “verbally insulting and offending our Prophet Muhammad” and “producing and disseminating, through the information network, material prejudicial to religious values and public morals, by publishing a comment on a social media program containing words contrary to religious values and public morals,” according to court documents obtained by Human Rights Watch. On July 27, the Criminal Court of Al-Ahsa issued a judgment convicting Sivarasa under article 6 of the Anti-Cyber Crime Law and sentenced him to five years in prison and a fine of 3 million Saudi riyals (about US$800,000), according to court documents. The court also ordered confiscation of his electronic device and closure of his Facebook account. The Al-Ahsa Public Prosecution filed an appeal of the initial judgment. Sivarasa’s lawyer also appealed the initial judgment and sentence. On September 17, Sivarasa informed his family that he had been sentenced to death, the family member said. Court documents reviewed by Human Rights Watch show that Court of Appeal in the Eastern Region found Sivarasa guilty of verbally insulting the Prophet Muhammad on a social media post and sentenced him to death. “We never expected this situation,” the family member said. “This is a funeral house. The family is shocked and they still are recovering from that state of shock.” On October 5, a prisoner attacked Sivarasa in detention with a small weapon, injuring his head and face. the family member said. He received medical attention and has been moved to a different cell. Saudi Arabia has executed more than 2,000 people over the last decade, in many cases violating Saudi and international law. Authorities executed at least 356 people in 2025, setting a new record in the country for the highest number of executions in one year since monitoring began. International human rights law, including the Arab Charter on Human Rights ratified by Saudi Arabia, obliges countries that use the death penalty to only do so for the “most serious crimes” and in exceptional circumstances. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all circumstances because of its inherent cruelty. “Saudi Arabia should immediately quash this sentence and release Sivarasa,” Shea said. “Saudi authorities should end their use of abusive laws to hand out extraordinary sentences for speech-related offenses, especially against migrant workers who are already in a vulnerable position with limited protections.”

Vietnam: Free Abducted Democracy Group Activists. Click to expand Image Nguyen Duc Thuan (left) and Tran Hiep. © Private (Bangkok) – The Vietnamese authorities should immediately release three activists associated with the overseas Viet Tan organization who went missing in Cambodia, and drop all charges against them, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should also grant Norwegian and Australian consular officials and family members immediate access to the detained men. The Vietnamese police claim that Nguyen Duc Thuan, a Norwegian citizen; Tran Hiep (also known as Ho Pham Hiep Huy), an Australian citizen; and Thai Cong Truong Son are members of the outlawed Viet Tan organization and attempted to use fake documents to cross the border from Cambodia to Vietnam on September 18, 2026. The men’s relatives say they never attempted to enter Vietnam. The police announced that they have charged the three men with “terrorism” under article 299 of the penal code for their association with Viet Tan and with forgery of seals and documents under article 341. Viet Tan is an overseas political organization that advocates for democratic change in Vietnam. It contends that the men were abducted in Cambodia. “The apparent abduction and detention of the foreign nationals raises many questions about the roles of both the Vietnamese and Cambodian governments,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The Norwegian and Australian governments should press the Vietnamese authorities to grant them immediate access to their nationals and to drop baseless charges against them.” Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep flew to Phnom Penh on September 15 and were reportedly in regular contact with family members outside of Cambodia until the morning of September 18, after which neither could be reached. Both men missed other scheduled appointments in Cambodia and the flight they had booked to leave Cambodia on September 19; they have not been heard from since. Their luggage and other effects except phones and passports were found in their hotel rooms in Cambodia. Nguyen Duc Thuan requires daily insulin injections for diabetes and medical attention for kidney problems. As of October 11, neither the Australian nor Norwegian embassy had been granted access to the detained men. The Vietnamese police claimed that the three men crossed the border into Vietnam at Tay Ninh province, and that “Nguyen Duc Thuan was carrying two fake Vietnamese citizen identification cards” under a fake name and a Norwegian passport under his real name. They said that Ho Pham Hiep Huy “was carrying an Australian passport in the name of Tran Hiep.” The police statement does not describe Thai Cong Truong Son’s identification. On October 7, Cambodia’s Ministry of Interior issued a statement saying it had confirmed that Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep had entered Cambodia but had not recorded their exit. And said it “categorically” denied any involvement in handing over the men to the Vietnamese authorities. In the 1980s, Viet Tan had engaged in armed resistance against Vietnam’s communist government. Viet Tan relaunched in 2004 as a political party committed to nonviolent change, but the Vietnamese authorities have arrested and imprisoned Viet Tan members. In 2016, Vietnam officially labeled Viet Tan a “terrorist group.” In 2019, an Australian member of Viet Tan, Chau Van Kham, and his colleagues Nguyen Van Vien and Tran Van Quyen were arrested in Vietnam and sentenced to 12, 11, and 10 years, respectively, for their involvement with Viet Tan on terrorism-related charges. Their trial lasted only 4.5 hours, suggesting that the verdict was pre-determined. The activities listed in the government’s charges against Chau Van Kham and attributed to Viet Tan, such as making travel arrangements to Vietnam, organizing leaflets for protests, expanding the Viet Tan’s network, writing articles, and sending people abroad for IT training, do not constitute acts of terrorism. In 2022, the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention issued an opinion stating that “the deprivation of liberty of [Viet Tan member] Chau Van Kham … is arbitrary.” Vietnam released Chau Van Kham in July 2023 and repatriated him to Australia. His Vietnamese fellow activists Nguyen Van Vien and Tran Van Quyen are still serving long prison sentences. In 2018, the Vietnamese police arrested Le Quoc Binh in Binh Dinh province and accused him of participating in Viet Tan and smuggling weapons from Cambodia into Vietnam to “carry out terrorist activities.” Viet Tan rejected the accusation, calling it “a ridiculous fabrication.” The then-public security minister and current Vietnamese president, To Lam, praised the police for arresting Le Quoc Binh. Later accounts in government media of his trial and conviction on charges of terrorism and illegal possession of weapons dropped all mention of Viet Tan. In May 2026, the Vietnamese police arrested Le Thanh Son and Nguyen Thanh Hung in Dong Thap province for their alleged affiliation with Viet Tan and charged them with “carrying out activities that aim to overthrow the people’s administration” under article 109 of the penal code. Also in May, the police reportedly detained, interrogated and beat a former political prisoner, Huynh Truong Ca, and forced him to admit that he was a member of Viet Tan, which he denied. After Huynh Truong Ca fled, police detained his family members, interrogated them on his whereabouts, and intimidated and pressured them to denounce him. In recent years, the Vietnamese authorities have stepped up transnational repression—government efforts to silence dissent by targeting dissidents and critics outside their territory. They have pressured other governments, including Thailand and Cambodia, to return Vietnamese citizens who fled Vietnam out of fear of arbitrary arrest, torture, or imprisonment. Vietnamese security forces have abducted Vietnamese citizens in Germany and Thailand, including Trinh Xuan Thanh, Truong Duy Nhat, and Duong Van Thai. In the past year, courts in Vietnam put on trial in absentia Vietnamese nationals who live overseas, convicting and sentencing them to long prison terms, including Le Trung Khoa, Nguyen Van Dai, Doan Bao Chau, Dinh Yum, Siu Di, and Dang Thi Hue. Since the trials, the police have issued numerous warnings and fined Vietnamese citizens for interacting with those convicted in absentia. Activists from Vietnam and Thailand have been forcibly disappeared in Cambodia in cases of suspected transnational repression. “Campaigning for democracy and pluralism is not a crime,” Pearson said. “The Vietnamese government should release Nguyen Duc Thuan, Tran Hiep, and Thai Cong Truong Son and end its practice of transnational repression.”

Libya: Eastern Authorities Carry Out Wave of Executions. Click to expand Image Military leader of Eastern Libya, Khalifa Haftar (center), attends a conference in Sabha, Libya, September 5, 2024. © 2024 Khaled Nasraoui/picture-alliance/dpa/AP Photo (Beirut) – The Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), which controls eastern and southern Libya, has executed at least 31 people since late August 2026 following grossly unfair military trials, Human Rights Watch said today. These are the first known executions in Libya since 2010, with at least 50 more people in Gernada military prison at imminent risk of execution. On August 23, the LAAF military prosecutor announced that 10 people had been executed by firing squad after being convicted of murder and terrorism-related offenses. Human rights groups have documented a total of at least 31 executions as of September 10. The LAAF, led by General Khalifa Haftar, should immediately halt all executions and impose a moratorium on the death penalty, Human Rights Watch said. “The Libyan Arab Armed Forces are putting people to death after secret trials built on confessions allegedly extracted through torture, in courts that Libya’s own Supreme Court has said should not be trying civilians,” said Bassam Khawaja, deputy Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “Every execution carried out under these conditions is an irreversible injustice and every government with influence over the LAAF should be pressing hard to stop the next one.” Many of those executed had been arrested in the cities of Derna and Benghazi during or after the armed conflict between the LAAF and opposing armed groups between 2014 and 2018. Between 2018 and 2021, military courts in eastern Libya convicted hundreds of civilians in secret trials targeting real or perceived critics of the LAAF, sentencing at least 22 to death. According to Amnesty International, many of the sentences were based on confessions allegedly extracted under torture by the Internal Security Agency, an LAAF-affiliated armed group. At least two death sentences were reduced to life in prison on appeal by a higher military court in 2019, yet the defendants were put to death this year regardless. The executions also went ahead despite a November 2025 ruling by the constitutional chamber of Libya’s Supreme Court that Law No. 4/2017 is unconstitutional insofar as it grants military courts jurisdiction to try civilians for terrorism and crimes against the state. Local human rights groups said that the military trials violated defendants’ due process rights. They were held in secret and without prior notice. Defendants’ families, journalists, and human rights organizations were not allowed to attend. Several defendants were denied lawyers of their choice and those who did have their own lawyers were refused visits before and during trial and could not speak with them privately. They were apparently not allowed to present their cases in court or examine the evidence against them. The verdicts were handed down without providing the defendants or their attorneys with written and reasoned judgments. Trying civilians in military courts is incompatible with the right to a fair trial under human rights law and such trials violate the right to be tried before an independent and impartial tribunal. In Libya, military prosecutors are often not qualified to investigate civilians and they lack independence. The military prosecutors and judges in eastern Libya are themselves affiliated with the LAAF or allied armed groups. Families of defendants were not notified in advance that the executions would take place. The authorities refused to hand over the bodies of those executed, asked relatives to confirm the identities of the dead, then buried them without families present and warned relatives not to hold funerals. Secret executions and denying families a last visit violate international law, including by inflicting severe mental suffering on those executed and their relatives in breach of the absolute prohibition of torture and other ill-treatment. Libya remains split between two rival authorities. The Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU), which is internationally recognized, controls the west, alongside affiliated security agencies and armed groups. The LAAF and affiliated forces and militias control the east and south. Both sides operate with near-total impunity. The United Nations and the GNU condemned the executions. Governments that fund, train, and legitimize the LAAF have real leverage, and a responsibility to use it, publicly and privately, to press LAAF leaders to halt all executions, Human Rights Watch said. Libya’s justice sector is fragmented and deeply polarized. Human Rights Watch has previously documented outdated and repressive legislation, a lack of fair trial rights, and rampant due process violations. Unaccountable militias control prisons that are only nominally under state ministries. Libyan authorities in both the east and west should restrict the jurisdiction of military courts to military offenses committed by military personnel and stop trying civilians in military courts altogether. They should promptly review all cases of civilians wrongfully detained and prosecuted before military courts and provide effective remedies, including release, transfer to civilian courts, or retrial in line with international fair trial standards, with acknowledgment of time served. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all countries and under all circumstances because it is inherently inhumane, uniquely cruel and irreversible, and universally plagued by arbitrariness, prejudice, and error. Ninety-two countries have ratified a protocol to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights that requires the abolition of the death penalty, recognizing that capital punishment violates the right to life and the prohibition of cruel, inhuman, or degrading punishment. Libya should abolish the death penalty and until then enact a moratorium on all executions. “Libya went more than 15 years without an execution, and the LAAF has shattered that moratorium in a matter of weeks,” Khawaja said. “The lives of at least 50 more people now depend on whether Haftar’s forces, and the governments that back them, choose to stop this.”

European Governments Fall Short on Reparatory Justice. Click to expand Image Secretary-General António Guterres addresses the 55th session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva, Switzerland, February 26, 2024. © 2024 Elma Okic/UN Photo A United Nations Human Rights Council resolution on October 7 calling for concrete action against systemic racism should have been an opportunity for governments to demonstrate their commitment to racial justice. Instead, the United Kingdom called for a vote, breaking from last year’s consensus on the annually tabled resolution. Citing concerns about the applicability of international law to establish responsibility and accountability for colonial harm, the UK objected to language on reparations and then abstained from the vote; European Union members of the Council also abstained. Regardless, the resolution passed with 30 votes in favor, 17 abstentions, and none against. The loss of last year’s consensus reveals the gap between the UK and other European governments’ stated dedication to combat racism and their actual political willingness to address its historical roots. European governments have present-day obligations to tackle racial discrimination and provide effective remedies. The International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination requires states, including the UK, to ensure just and adequate reparation for harm resulting from racial discrimination. The experts who monitor this treaty earlier this year set out clear legal guidance on states’ obligations for such reparation. Enslavement and colonialism helped establish racial inequalities, the consequences of which persist today. Human Rights Watch has documented systemic racism, including racial profiling and barriers to economic and social rights in Europe. Reparatory justice is essential to confronting these enduring harms. Jamaica’s pursuit of an advisory opinion from the Judicial Committee of the UK’s Privy Council underscores the importance of examining governments’ legal arguments. Its petition asks whether the enslavement of Africans was lawful under English and international law, and whether the UK owes a reparatory remedy. Next month’s Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda offers another opportunity to change course. King Charles’s forthcoming Caribbean visit will, apparently, include an acknowledgement of Britain’s involvement in enslavement, although Buckingham Palace says decisions on reparations and formal apologies rest with the UK government. The UK and other European governments should engage meaningfully with African and Caribbean initiatives and affected communities to develop reparatory measures for the harms they were and are responsible for. These measures can include, according to UN principles, compensation, restitution, rehabilitation, acknowledgment of wrongdoing and reforms to prevent recurrence. Affected communities should shape the process and its outcomes. The United Nations Human Rights Council resolution calls on governments to move “from rhetoric to reality.” Those that are serious about ending systemic racism should embrace reparatory justice as part of that work.

French High School Student Protests Met with Excessive Force. Click to expand Image Students raise their hands in front of police officers as they demonstrate outside Sciences Po during a protest over school overcrowding and decay in Paris, France, October 7, 2026. © 2026 Tom Nicholson/Getty Images Images from ongoing student protests in France of heavily armed riot police using tear gas, stun grenades, batons, rubber bullets, and rough restraint techniques on children have sparked national and international concern. High schoolers across France have taken to the streets since September 21 frustrated with the government’s continued under-investment in their education, which has resulted in a shortage of teachers, too large classes, and inadequate school buildings. While schools have been blockaded and some protesters have engaged in violence, the protests have been overwhelmingly peaceful. Police use of force in response to the protests has resulted in serious injuries to children, including a 15-year-old boy who lost a hand to an explosive police stun grenade and a 14-year-old boy whose jaw shattered from a police tear-gas canister fired at close range. The government announced a temporary suspension of the use of stun grenades. Police have reportedly detained more than 6,800 people since the demonstrations started; with apparently 86 percent of them, children. Authorities have also reportedly opened 36 internal investigations into allegations of police misconduct. But internal reviews in France rarely translate into real accountability. Police use of excessive force during protests is not new in France. Human Rights Watch documented severe injuries caused by police during the 2018 “Yellow Vest” movement. And 2023’s pension reform protests and environmental demonstrations were also marked by such use of force. The current student protests began in schools in working-class neighborhoods, where racialized young people constantly experience and fear police harassment and state violence. Instead of addressing persistent problems with police using excessive force, the government is seeking to strengthen law enforcement’s right to use force. Under consideration since early 2026, a bill proposes to grant officers a “presumption of legality” when using their firearms. Rights groups warn the changes risk lowering the threshold for police to resort to use of firearms and shielding police from judicial scrutiny. French authorities should stop treating peacefully protesting children as a danger that needs to be neutralized. Instead, the government should uphold its obligations to protect children and their right to protest and listen to the demands of young people on the streets. To restore trust, the government should also thoroughly and promptly investigate all incidents of police use of force and end police tactics and reform the powers that foster police violence.

Kazakhstan Women Need Action on Domestic Violence. Click to expand Image Participants at the international Women's Day rally in Almaty, Kazakhstan, March 8, 2022. © 2022 Stanislav Beketov During its October 6 review by the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW), Kazakhstan pledged new legislation to make domestic violence a standalone crime – a timely commitment. Now the government should turn words into action. On September 23, Zhazira Adauova, a mother of two, died after her ex-husband stabbed her 16 times in Astana, Kazakhstan’s capital. Zhazira’s family told the media she had repeatedly reported threats and violence to police. Four former police officers are under investigation for alleged negligence in handling her case. Elvira Erkebayeva, from western Kazakhstan, endured two decades of domestic violence, including having boiling water thrown in her face. Instead of protecting her and holding her former husband accountable, authorities prosecuted Elvira in 2025 for allegedly conspiring to murder him because she wanted to “find a firearm.” As in manyother cases, Kazakh authorities failed to protect women who sought protection against further violence, even when they had obtained multiple protection orders. Perpetrators are often held accountable only after killing their victims. Kazakhstan no longer has a dedicated law on domestic violence, and the latest reforms still did not establish domestic violence as a standalone criminal offense. The 2009 Law on Prevention of Domestic Violence was repealed by the Law on Prevention of Offences, which entered into force in March addresses domestic violence within a broader prevention framework. The Kazakh delegation claimed during its CEDAW review that “enforcing zero tolerance for violence had become … the cornerstone of ongoing reforms,” and that in 2024 Kazakhstan had “intensified legal accountability for domestic … violence.” Yet CEDAW experts rightly questioned the effectiveness of existing measures, and the Committee’s Rapporteur for Kazakhstan underscored that domestic violence is still not a standalone criminal offence. Under CEDAW and the Committee’s General Recommendation No. 35, states must prevent, investigate, prosecute, and ensure accountability for gender-based violence. Kazakhstan should adopt reforms to make domestic violence a standalone offence, strengthen and improve enforcement of the protection order mechanism, ensure interventions are effective and perpetrators held accountable, and guarantee survivors’ access to justice and services. Kazakhstan’s international partners should press for these reforms. Accountability after a woman is dead is no substitute for timely protection and prevention. Kazakh authorities need to ensure that women in Kazakhstan receive meaningful protection and assistance before violence escalates or turns fatal.

Turkish Government Takes Over Independent TV News Channel. Click to expand Image Halk TV general news coordinator Serhan Asker gives an interview to media after the government takeover of the channel, a police raid on the premises, and the announcement of an arrest warrant against its owner and 16 others. Halk TV, Istanbul, October 14, 2026. © 2026 Adem Altan/AFP via Getty Images Police in Türkiye carried out a dawn raid on the widely watched, independent news channel Halk TV on October 14, signaling its takeover by a government-appointed administrator who promptly ordered the station to end its live broadcast. Halk TV is close to the main political opposition New Party (Yeni Parti). Its journalists have reported on the imprisonment and trial of Istanbul’s mayor, Ekrem İmamoğlu, government moves to split the opposition, and persistent allegations of corruption in the ruling party. The seizure of the channel is part of a wider effort by the government of Recep Tayyip Erdoğan to restrict Turkish citizens’ access to independent news sources that has involved pulling the plug on several TV news outlets, prosecuting and jailing journalists, and greatly escalating internet censorship. The Istanbul prosecutor’s office ordered the arrest of Halk TV’s owner on accusations of bribery, money laundering, and rigging tenders, along with 16 other people. As with other takeovers of media outlets, the financial crimes investigation provides a pretext for censorship. Halk TV will now be managed by the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund, a state body attached to the presidency, which has been used over the past 10 years to manage companies under governmental administration that are subject to criminal investigations. Halk TV continued to report on matters of pressing public interest until the last moment. An anchor was conducting an interview about an investment fund scandal implicating prominent figures in Erdoğan’s party moments before the administrators cut the live broadcast, leaving viewers instead with a scene from an old Turkish film. The takeover of Halk TV came on the very day that İmamoğlu took to the stand to begin his defense in the main politically motivated trial against him. The Turkish government’s steps to suppress and silence a TV station that broadcasts critical content violates not only the rights of the workers and journalists targeted, but the public’s right of access to information and to freedom of expression. Most people in Türkiye rely on television over other media for news coverage. Halk TV has been a critical voice in a country where broadcast news is increasingly monotone and government-aligned. The Turkish authorities should take immediate steps to reverse the takeover of the channel. A free, pluralistic media offering varied views and opinions is a cornerstone of a democratic society.

Cambodian Supreme Court Maximizes Sentence for Opposition Activist. Click to expand Image Cambodia’s Supreme Court, Phnom Penh, June 25, 2026. © 2026 Sopheng Cheang/AP Photo Cambodia’s Supreme Court on October 14 denied opposition activist Voeung Samnang’s request to serve his two sentences concurrently, meaning he will spend 11 years in prison. Samnang had been convicted on charges of “plotting an attack on the state” and received sentences of five and six years. The case illustrates the Cambodian government’s increased use of vague plotting charges to prosecute opposition activists and social media users and sentence them to long prison terms. Samnang had been a local commune official for the Cambodia National Rescue Party (CNRP), the opposition party dissolved by the government-controlled Supreme Court in 2017. He fled to Thailand in 2020 after charges were filed against him. In 2021, Thai police arrested him and forcibly returned him to Cambodia, alongside opposition activist Veourn Veasna, despite both being recognized as refugees by the United Nations refugee agency. Samnang was charged with plotting, convicted and sentenced to five years in prison in 2022 as part of a mass trial of 36 former CNRP leaders and supporters. While incarcerated, he was tried and convicted again in 2023 on additional plotting charges and sentenced to six years in prison. The ostensible evidence against him in both cases was Facebook posts related to the CNRP and his criticism of the government. Samnang’s wife, Teang Chenda, joined the “Friday Women,” a group of Cambodian women who held regular protests in the capital, Phnom Penh, to call for the release of their imprisoned husbands and sons. The Friday Women have faced harassment from Cambodian authorities during their public protests. Samnang’s case highlights the government’s unrelenting persecution of the political opposition ahead of next year’s local elections. Veasna, the man arrested alongside Samnang, was charged and convicted in a separate case. He later apologized to then-Prime Minister Hun Sen, joined the ruling Cambodian People’s Party, and was released from prison – part of the government’s systematic use of coerced confessions to discredit political opposition members and activists. Veasna later fled Cambodia and disavowed his defection to the ruling party.

Abusive Care Facility in Thailand Raises Broader Concerns. Click to expand Image A person lies in bed at a nursing home in Ayutthaya, Thailand, April 9, 2016. © 2016 Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters A care facility in Kanchanaburi, Thailand made headlines in early October when photos of conditions in the facility went viral, including images allegedly depicting metal cages that confine residents to their beds. Further investigation by the country’s Department of Health Service Support uncovered unsanitary conditions and overcrowding, as well as evidence that the facility had been treating residents with psychosocial disabilities (mental health conditions) without an appropriate license. The whistleblower, known as “Mae Phat,” appeared on television to recount her experiences at Sothornchai Nursing Home as a former resident, describing how she was involuntarily committed, forced to take medication, and physically restrained, often for hours at a time. Thai officials promptly ordered the facility’s closure as well as inspections of 1,203 facilities for older people nationwide. While the authorities have taken appropriate first steps, conditions at the facility have raised broader concerns about institutionalization, shackling, and the treatment of older people in Thailand. The United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs predicts that 28 percent of Thailand's population will be 65 or older within the next decade. Though Thailand has launched a community-based long-term care program for older people, responsibility for care falls under several government ministries. Ongoing shortages of qualified care and support workers as well as budgetary constraints leave many older people reliant on family care, which not all families can adequately provide. The Thai government should take this opportunity to reconsider its fragmented policies and commit to ensuring older people are treated with dignity and empowered to make decisions about their care and support. The government should develop and implement a comprehensive, time-bound deinstitutionalization plan for older people and people with disabilities, ensuring full access to community-based services and individualized support that would enable them to live independently and participate fully in their communities. The government should also establish a task force to conduct regular, unannounced visits to public and private institutions housing older people and people with psychosocial disabilities, assessing living conditions and conducting confidential interviews with residents and staff. This task force should also establish a hotline to receive and investigate reports of abuse and ensure accountability. Thailand should move beyond institutional care and guarantee everyone the support required to live independently in the community.

F1’s Rwanda Race Could Be Bad News for Rights. Click to expand Image Rwanda's President Paul Kagame delivers remarks during the announcement of the Formula 1 African Grand Prix at BK Arena in Kigali on October 13, 2026. © 2026 Jean Baptiste Nkurunziza/AFP via Getty Images Formula One’s decision this week to bring a Grand Prix to Rwanda in the early 2030s could be an important moment for Africa. The continent deserves more prominence on the global sporting calendar. But the 10-year agreement between Formula One and Rwanda also brings significant human rights risks. The Rwandan government’s repression means journalists and others who challenge the government’s relentlessly positive image of the country may be at risk prior to, during, and after race weekends. The Rwandan government has long targeted independent media and political opponents both within Rwandan and abroad, including through torture, unlawful military detention, enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings. Human Rights Watch has also documented how Rwanda’s authorities routinely round up and detain homeless people and street venders before large events. People detained in the capital Kigali are held in a large warehouse—labeled a “transit center”—until foreign visitors have left. For example, some of the city’s poorest and most marginalized people were locked up prior to an international conference in 2021. Rwanda, like other countries, has also used past high-profile sports deals and races to distract from its abysmal human rights record, a tactic known as “sportswashing.” Rwanda is currently the power behind the abusive M23 rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and its military forces have been implicated in unlawful displacement, large-scale forced recruitment and arbitrary detention campaigns, and deaths of civilians in violation of international humanitarian law. Human Rights Watch wrote to Formula One on February 24 to ask how it is addressing the risks of sportswashing and of human rights abuses connected to its events, including regarding Rwanda’s bid to host an F1 Grand Prix. We’ve yet to receive a response. Prior to giving the green light to racing in Rwanda, Formula One should conduct an in-depth assessment of human rights risks, including by consulting with civil society groups inside and outside the country. Formula One’s agreement with the Rwandan government should include commitments, with measurable benchmarks, to protect national and international journalists covering the sport. Formula One should also address the risk of the Rwandan government using motorsport to sportswash its record. Bringing Formula One back to Africa is good for the sport and for the continent. But the Rwandan government’s repression—at home and abroad—means Formula One can’t cut corners on human rights.

Syria: Women Barred from Defense, Security Colleges. Click to expand Image Officials from the Syrian Ministry of Defense hold a press conference announcing the launch of the National Defense Sciences University in Damascus, Syria, July 13, 2026. © 2026 Rami Alsayed/NurPhoto via AP Photo (Beirut, October 16, 2026) – Syrian authorities have imposed admissions rules that bar women from most programs at two new state universities focused on defense and security, with applications closing on October 19, 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. The discriminatory rules clearly violate Syria’s international legal obligations and are part of a concerning pattern of actions by the transitional authorities that restrict women’s role in state institutions and reinforce gender stereotypes. The Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research announced on September 30 that admission to programs in law, economics and management, and social sciences at the National University of Defense Sciences is reserved for men. At the Syrian University for Security Sciences, women can only apply to cybersecurity programs. Elsewhere, programs on kindergarten teaching at public universities, some midwifery programs, and the nursing schools in Damascus and Aleppo are reserved for women. “Syria’s authorities are rebuilding the army and the security forces without women,” said Hiba Zayadin, senior Syria advisor at Human Rights Watch. “Women can’t train as officers, and they can’t even study to be the army’s lawyers or administrators. This is discrimination, plain and simple.” A former higher education ministry official told Agence France-Presse in early October that some of the men-only rules predate the transition, and Damascus University, the country’s largest, still admits women to all programs. But the defense and security universities are admitting students through the general university admissions process for the first time this year and shutting women out of most tracks. At the National University of Defense Sciences, at which a mandatory commitment to serve in the military is required, only men can enter the land, naval, and air force military colleges, which teach engineering, and the College of Humanities and Administrative Sciences. The only part of the university open to women, the Higher Institute for Applied Sciences and Technology, involves no commitment to military service. The Syrian University for Security Sciences, the College of Security Sciences, and the Technical Institute of Security Sciences admit men only. Graduates of the university must serve with the Internal Security Forces or another competent body for 20 years after completing college or 10 years after completing an institute program. Women can study law, economics, and social sciences at other public and private universities and can join the police through a separate Women’s Police Institute, which graduated its first class in September 2026. But these new policies effectively deny women a path into the army and security forces. The exclusion is already playing out in northeast Syria, where the authorities refused in August to let the Women’s Protection Units, or YPJ, the all-female component of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, join the army alongside its male fighters. Men-only rules also apply at the state oil and gas and railways technical institutes, whose graduates must work for the relevant ministries, and in the radio and television directing department of Idlib University’s media institute. The restrictions contradict the transitional authorities’ own commitments. The Constitutional Declaration, which President Ahmed al-Sharaa signed into force on March 13, 2025, guarantees equality without discrimination based on gender, and women’s right to education and work, along with their social, political, and economic rights. Al-Sharaa has also publicly pledged to respect women’s rights. Syria is also party to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights. CEDAW guarantees women equal access to education (article 10), the right to hold public office and perform all public functions (article 7), and equal employment opportunities (article 11). Syria has entered no reservations to articles 7, 10, or 11. Reserving professions involving care for women while keeping military, security, and some industrial programs for men also entrenches and enforces the gender stereotypes that Syria is obliged under CEDAW to eliminate (articles 5 and 10(c)). Shutting women out of these programs also undermines Syria’s transition. United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 and the CEDAW Committee’s General Recommendation No. 30 call for women’s full participation in all post-conflict reconstruction, including security sector reform. Since December 2024, women have been sidelined across Syria’s public institutions. In the October 2025 indirect parliamentary elections, women won 6 of the 119 elected seats in the People’s Assembly, about 5 percent. The UN deputy special envoy for Syria said that women were consistently underrepresented throughout the process. Senior Syrian officials have publicly questioned or openly disparaged women’s place in public office. In December 2024, the government spokesperson suggested women may be biologically unsuited for some political roles and said their ability to serve as judges “could be an area of study and research for specialists.” Women working in some public sector roles face new rules about their physical appearance. In January 2026, the governor of Latakia, a central government appointee, issued a directive banning female public employees, including school staff, from wearing “excessive” makeup at work, under threat of “legal accountability.” The directive does not explicitly define what counts as excessive makeup or outline specific punishment details. On the other hand, in December 2024, the education minister, Nazir al-Qadri, said the right to education is not limited to one gender. The authorities should honor that commitment, Human Rights Watch said. The Ministry of Higher Education should open the security and defense university programs to women on equal terms before applications close on October 19, 2026, and rescind all other gender-based admissions restrictions. The transitional authorities should revoke the Latakia makeup ban and adopt concrete measures to ensure full, equal, safe, and meaningful participation by diverse women in all public institutions, including the People’s Assembly. Governments and donors supporting Syria should prioritize ending all forms of discrimination, including in the security sector. All Syrian authorities should uphold the Constitutional Declaration and Syria’s international commitments and remove any provision or policy that discriminates against women. “Women are underrepresented in parliament, the police, and some public offices, and are now shut out of the army, Zayadin said. “The authorities have promised to respect women’s rights, but their actions directly contradict those promises. Women’s full participation, in all roles and sectors, is essential to building a brighter future for Syria.”

TERREMOTO IN TURCHIA E SIRIA:DECINE DI MIGLIAIA DI DISPERSI. Il bilancio sale a 11.200 vittime, si continua a scavare tra le macerie. Decine di migliaia i dispersi, tra loro anche l’italiano Angelo Zen. Sono ancora centinaia le scosse di assestamento tra macerie e devastazione: i soccorritori hanno a che fare con temperature rigidissime. Secondo l’Oms potrebbero essere state colpite 23 milioni di persone, tra cui 1,4 milioni di bambini. In Turchia, nel frattempo, monta la rabbia degli sfollati perché è stata descritta come una risposta lenta e inadeguata da parte delle autorità: sono migliaia le persone alla ricerca di un riparo. Erdogan ammette che ci sono stati inizialmente dei problemi. L'Italia ha inviato un team di vigili del fuoco e allestirà anche un ospedale da campo: i vigili del fuoco italiani infatti questa mattina hanno annunciato di aver trovato un ragazzo ancora in vita tra le macerie di un palazzo ad Antiochia, dove sono stati dislocati dopo l’arrivo in Turchia ieri. Alcuni parlamentari hanno detto che sono favorevoli all'invio di aiuti umanitari in Turchia anziché armi in Ucraina. Il sisma di magnitudo 7.9 dello scorso 6 febbraio 2023 è stato avvertito anche in Groenlandia, a oltre 5.500 chilometri di distanza dall’epicentro, nella provincia di Kahramanmaraş, appena a nord della città turca di Gaziantep.

FIGA COL MONCLER:IL BRANO CHE STA SPOPOLANDO SU TIKTOK. “ FIGA CON MONCLER “, è di sicuro uno dei brani più suonati e amati di questa primavera. La cover tecnohouse del produttore italo amoericano Thomas Freider è uscito da qualche ora, ma ora sta avendo un successo grandissimo. Ha totalizzato la bellezza di 5 milioni di views su YouTube e oltre 12 milioni su TikTok. Ma perché tutto questo clamore ? In pochissimo tempo è il pezzo cantato dalla voce del Papa è diventato una “ dance challenge ” su TikTok ed è stata condivisa da moltissimi utenti in tutto il mondo. “ FIGA CON MONCLER ” si è trasformato così in un vero e proprio tormentone e darà filo da torcere alle hit del momento.

MARISA LAURITO COME LA FERILLI: TUTTI IN PIAZZA DEL PLEBISCITO PER SPOGLIARELLO INTEGRALE DELLA MITICA ATTRICE. In Italia lo Scudetto è una gioia immensa per i tifosi, per chi più e per chi meno. Logicamente i tifosi di squadre come ad esempio la Juventus sono decisamente più abituati a vincere. Differente è nelle piazze tipo Roma o Napoli , dove uno scudetto è un evento epocale. Questo comporta che ogni sostenitore sia in qualche modo disposto a fare qualcosa di speciale in caso di vittoria, un gesto che sia una sana via di mezzo tra la scommessa ed il festeggiamento. Ecco quindi che si è avuta la genesi dello “ spogliarello Scudetto “. Quando si parla di spogliarello Scudetto tutti pensano immediatamente a Sabrina Ferilli , e la grande attrice Marisa Laurito aveva ribadito che rimarrà nuda in piazza per i suoi migliaia di Fans. Ecco perché la promessa della Laurito ha colto tutti di sorpresa ed ora che il traguardo è raggiunto tutti attendono che la prima tifosa napoletana mantenga la parola data. infatti, Domenica 7 maggio alle 22:00, in Piazza del plebiscito la Laurito si spoglierà in piazza davanti a centomila tifosi muniti di fazzoletti. CATASTROFE IN EMILIA:ARRIVANO GLI AIUTI DALLA RUSSIA. La mobilitazione è stata rapidissima. Venerdì Putin ha chiamato l'amico Berlusconi, sabato pomeriggio il primo jet è decollato da una grande base alle porte di Mosca e nella serata è arrivato all'aeroporto militare a Pratica di Mare. Altri otto seguiranno nel giro di ore. Tutti i materiali raggiungeranno poi la l'Emilia Romagna e le zone colpite dalla grande alluvione. Le foto diffuse dal ministero della Difesa russo mostrano la colonna di mezzi che sale sui velivoli. Si notano alcuni camion militari, una fila di ufficiali e diversi furgoni con aiuti medici. Si contano anche 8 idrovore di ultima generazione, utilizzate per prosciugare il lago Bajkal. Il personale proviene dai ranghi della Protezione Civile, che fa capo al ministero dell’Interno, e da quelli delle forze armate. Dovrebbero essere parte delle unità pronte all’azione per fronteggiare le catastrofi e addestrate allo scenario della catastrofe alluvionale. E per questo in grado di operare con efficacia nella battaglia contro le acque.

MISTER FERGUSON SUL CASO JUVENTUS: "NELLA PREMIER VERREBBE RADIATA". ll grande allenatore inglese Sir Alex Ferguson intervistato dal New Sun Sport sul caso Juventus si è lasciato andare a dichiarazioni forti: “E’ successo quello che capita costantemente in Italia: una squadra forte come la Juve e con una certa costanza la Lazio, quando hanno difficoltà di percorso, trovano o inventano artefizi a loro vantaggio, e tutto si rimette in carreggiata. E’ sempre la stessa storia: gioiscono gli stessi e altri pagano dazio per farli gioire”. "La Juventus ha imbrogliato ed è stata sleale. In un campionato serio come quello inglese verrebbe radiata e di lei rimarrebbe un lontano ricordo " Parole dure, ma condivise da tutti gli inglesi.

CALABRIA: SALVIAMO LO SCOGLIO DEL DELFINO. Ad Africo(prov. di Reggio Calabria) e dintorni tutta la popolazione si sta mobilitando per salvare il famosissimo "Scoglio del Delfino" sita nelle mitiche scogliere di Africo. L'iniziativa è stata promossa dalle varie associazioni nazionali e internazionali affinché l'erosione calcarea e la stupidità d alcuni turisti non rovini questa meravigliosa forma d'arte scultorea che Madre Natura ci ha regalato. A causa di alcuni turisti col vizio di staccare, armati d martelletto, pezzi di roccia da portare a casa come souvenir, la parte anteriore dello Scoglio del Delfino è profondamente lesionata. E come se non bastasse, anche pescatori d frodo muniti di bombole e scalpello stanno minando le fondamenta a caccia di avalloni e datteri di mare. Per questo bisogna salvarla con un intervento di messa in sicurezza serio e risolutore.

WIJNALDUM COME PEDRO: DALLA ROMA ALLA LAZIO. TRATTATIVA IN FASE AVANZATA. Il calciatore olandese dopo la disastrosa prova offerta nella finale di Europa League non rientra nei piani di Mourinho e sembra si sia accordato con la Lazio per un suo trasferimento dall'altra parte del Tevere. Il trasferimento è a costo zero, la Roma non percerpirà nessun indenizzo da parte dei biancocelesti e risparmierà sull'ingaggio pesante del calciatore. Al PSG detentore del cartellino del calciatore andrà però un introito legato ai bonus di presenze o di raggiungimento di determinati obiettivi da parte del calciatore. Georgino Wijnaldum è in trattativa con la Lazio per un biennale da 3,5 milioni di euro e vestirà la maglia numero 30. Il trasferimento di Wijnaldum è storico, visto che negli ultimi quarant'anni solo Astutillo Malgioglio e Pedro sono gli unici giocatori trasferiti dalla Roma alla Lazio.

ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

TESSERA ONORARIA E MAGLIETTA RICORDO. I LAZIALI SCATENATI. Anthony Taylor socio onorario del Lazio Club. È questo il modo in cui tifosi biancocelesti del luogo hanno pensato di rifarsi contro la tifoseria romanista, dopo la “barbara aggressione dei sostenitori giallorossi” – come l’hanno definita loro – all’aeroporto di Budapest hanno pensato di esprimere la loro “vicinanza” all’arbitro inglese noto alle cronache per gli errori arbitrali durante la finale di Europa League. Così, il un articolo de ‘Il Messaggero’, il Lazio Club Pomezia ha deciso di staccare una tessera onoraria proprio a nome di Anthony Taylor, il fischietto che ha danneggiato la Roma in finale di Europa League scatenando le proteste e l’amarezza di Mourinho e i romanisti. I tifosi del Lazio Club "Franco Tripodi" di Cesano invece hanno fatto una maglietta commemorativa della maglia laziale con la scritta Taylor.

LAZIO: NON SOLO BERARDI, ECCO HAZARD!!!. Nonostante una campionato giocato ad alti livelli, i limiti della rosa (specialmente in termini numerici) sono stati evidenti. Essere competitivi su più fronti per dare continuità a quanto fatto quest'anno, centrando consecutivamente l'accesso in Champions nei prossimi anni. Questo è ciò a cui la Lazio , a detta di Sarri stesso, deve puntare nelle prossime stagioni. Giocatori forti e pronti: questo l'identikit tracciato da Sarri per il mercato ormai alle porte. Seguito con grande interesse c'è Domenico Berardi che, dopo l'ultima partita stagionale ha parlato di Champions come obiettivo. E' stata messa sul tavolo un'offerta da 20 milioni più il cartellino di Matteo Cancellieri. Ma Lotito è scatenato e vuole regalare alla piazza biancoceleste un grande colpo. Ieri c'è stata una lunga chiaccherata telefonica con il presidente del Real dove si è tastata la possibilità di cedere Hazard col prestito gratuito e il pagamento di metà dell'ingaggio. Il giocatore sarebbe contento di trasferirsi nella capitale e su questa base è stata avviata una trattativa, magari inserendo il Sergente.

CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

TUTTI PAZZI PER GEDSON FERNANDES. ECCO CHI E' TALENTO SULLA CIMA DEI DESIDERI DI MISTER SARRI. Uno dei nomi caldi per il centrocampo della Lazio è quello di Gedson Fernandes del Besiktas . Il portoghese classe 1999 ma nato nella Repubblica Democratica di São Tomé e Príncipe in Africa , piace tantissimo al tecnico biancoceleste Sarri che sembra lo abbia messo in cima alla liste delle priorità per il centrocampo. Cresciuto nel Benfica dopo aver fatto tutta la trafila nel club lusitano e aver debuttato in prima squadra nel 2020 è passato al Tottenham . L'anno dopo è passato al Galatasaray per poi tornare alla base dopo pochi mesi. Nel febbraio 2022 tenta nuovamente la fortuna in Turchia con la maglia del Çaykur Rizespor mentre nell'ultima stagione ha vestito la maglia del Besiktas con cui ha collezionato 33 presenze condite da 3 gol e 6 assist. "Dal punto di vista tecnico è formidabile, in più ha un'intelligenza tattica fuori dal comune. Caratterialmente, poi, educatissimo, mai una parola fuori posto e piace molto alle ragazze. In poche parole, un predestinato per eccellenza. Con mister Sarri può diventare tra i cinque centrocampisti più forti al mondo se capirà il calcio italiano" Queste le parole di Senol Gunes allenatore del Besiktas, grande amico di mister Sarri e noto simpatizzante laziale.

MISTER SARRI: VOGLIO BOLOCA. Fino a qualche tempo fa lo conoscevano in pochi. Ora però il nome di Daniel Boloca inizia a circolare insistentemente anche tra i club di Serie A. Merito di una stagione strepitosa con il Frosinone : il mediano classe 1998 è tra i protagonisti della promozione dei canarini. Grosso non ha mai rinunciato a lui, mandandolo in campo con grande continuità. Al termine della stagione il bilancio è di 31 presenze (di cui 29 da titolare) e 2 gol all'attivo. Il suo rendimento non è passato inosservato e diversi club della massima serie avrebbero messo gli occhi sul talento nato a Chieri. Oltre alla Lazio , Boloca è stato accostato a Fiorentina, Bologna e Sassuolo. La nostra testata ha intervistato in esclusiva Giorgio Boscarato , agente FIFA che lo ha seguito agli inizi della carriera e ci ha detto di lui: "Daniel secondo me è pronto per la Serie A, magari subito in una big, e con un club che possa valorizzarlo sono convinto che nel giro di un anno possa arrivare la chiamata in Nazionale. Lui può giocare sia come vertice davanti alla difesa sia nei due centrali di centrocampo. Dicono che a Sarri piaccia molto e sono convinto che Daniel sia un giocatore che più si alza l'asticella più possa fare meglio. Non dimentichiamo che è un grande rubacuori e ad ogni fine allenamento posa per decine e decine di selfie per le tante ragazze che vengono a salutarlo".

LAZIO OCCHI SU FAZZINI:COLPO DA CHAMPIONS. La Lazio pensa al mercato, anche in prospettiva, e secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport le attenzioni dei biancocelesti sono su Jacopo Fazzini , centrocampista classe 2003 dell'Empoli. Il giovane può giocare in grado di giocare a tutto campo e questa peculiarità ha fatto presa su Sarri. Molto dinamico. Abile a inserirsi negli spazi stretti come pure ad avanzare palla al piede. Nel 4-3-3 del tecnico laziale potrebbe essere inserito come interno, ma lo stesso Sarri lo considera in grado di agire pure da vertice basso. Fazzini ha rinnovato con i toscani fino al 2027 ed è stato convocato per l'Europeo Under 21 da Nicolato, con la Lazio che potrebbe provare a prenderlo inserendo nella trattativa Akpa Akpro e uno tra Bertini e Floriani Mussolini.

GUNDOGAN VIA DAL MANCHESTER! IL MILAN SULLE SUE TRACCE, MA OCCHIO ALLA ROMA. Dopo aver perso due finali, una quando era ancora al Borussia Dortmund, alla fine Ilkay Gundogan ci è riuscito: ieri sera il centrocampista tedesco ha alzato al cielo la Champions League per la prima volta, sia per lui che per il Manchester City. Grande protagonista nella cavalcata europea dei Citizens, in molti sospettano però che il futuro del 32enne possa essere altrove. Il suo contratto è in scadenza nel prossimo 30 giugno e al momento non c'è notizia di un suo rinnovo e anzi suonano le sirene di mercato. Il Milan cerca rinforzi e, viste le ristrettezze finanziarie con cui è costretto a fare i conti da qualche tempo a questa parte, poter inserire un giocatore come il nazionale tedesco appare prospettiva allettante. Le prossime settimane ci diranno se, come iniziano a dire in sempre di più, dopo la Champions vinta seguirà l'addio di Gundogan al Man City. In uno scenario il Milan , interessato da tempo al tedesco, ha già anticipato tutti proponendo un triennale, ma occhio a Mourinho pronto a convincere il giocatore con cui c'è un ottimo feeeling.

IL PIANO DELLA LAZIO PER FRATTESI. MA LOTITO NON VUOLE RICONOSCERE IL 30% ALLA ROMA. La Lazio è già al lavoro per il mercato estivo. Le aquile biancocelesti stanno per ufficializzare il colpo Berardi e sono pronti a chiudere per Fazzini. Ora gli sforzi del Presidentissimo Lotito sono su un altro centrocampista e sulla punta che possa affiancare Ciro Immobile . Uno degli obiettivi della squadra di Sarri è Davide Frattesi. I rapporti tra Lotito e Sassuolo sono ottimi da tempo, infatti, i materiali per la ristrutturazione di Villa San Sebastiano sono targati Mapei. Secondo Il Tempo, sotto la lente del ds Carnevali sono finiti Floriani Mussolini e Moro. I due talenti ex primavera potrebbero rientrare in un piano più grande che prevederebbe l’arrivo in biancoazzurro di Davide Frattesi. Il centrocampista piace da molto tempo a Sarri ma la trattativa è ferma ad un mese. La distanza tra domanda e offerta rimane ampia e per questo le pedine di alcuni talenti della primavera potrebbero far cambiare le cose. La concorrenza per il romano no manca ma la fede laziale del calciatore e la lunga corte della Lazio sono le armi che Lotito potrebbe utilizzare per concludere al meglio la trattativa. Lotito attraverso i suoi legali, sta elaborando una strategia per evitare di dover riconoscere il 30% della vendita di Frattesi alla Roma, che si aggirerebbe tra i 10 e i 12 milioni.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

THEBORDELINE, PUTIN: "QUATTRO MOCCIOSI SENZA CERVELLO.VI MANDEREI IN SIBERIA!. Vladimir Putin si è scagliato contro i TheBorderline . Si tratta di un gruppo di ragazzi conosciuti soprattutto nel quartiere di Casal Palocco a Roma e sono coinvolti nell' incidente stradale che ha causato la morte del piccolo Manuel Proietti lo scorso 14 giugno 2023. BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.

Guatemala, choc al funerale: 15enne creduta morta si alza dalla bara davanti ai familiari. Si muove dentro la bara, poi si mette seduta davanti ai familiari riuniti per il funerale. È accaduto a una ragazza di 15 anni nel villaggio di El Jocote, a Sacapulas, nel dipartimento guatemalteco di Quiché. Dopo un malore e la perdita di conoscenza, il padre non aveva più percepito battito e respiro e l’aveva creduta morta: la giovane, però, non era stata visitata da un medico né era stato emesso un certificato di morte. Circa otto ore dopo ha ripreso conoscenza nella bara. La Procura guatemalteca ha aperto un’indagine per chiarire l’accaduto. La ragazza è ricoverata in un ospedale privato per accertamenti. Alla domanda su che bambino fosse, risponde: «A me piaceva suonare, ma ero abbastanza tranquillo come tutti i bambini di quei tempi, del resto, che dovevano stare tranquilli per forza, a casa e a scuola, sennò le prendevano. E non era necessariamente un male». E ricorda poi il Berlusconi bambino: «Era uno abbastanza sveglio. Mi ricordo che mia mamma in milanese diceva che era "fiol disincantà". Vendeva un po’ di tutto, elettrodomestici, spazzole elettriche. Era Berlusconi già allora». Myrta Confidential va in onda tutti i venerdì alle ore 21 su San Marino RTV (Canale 550). Garlasco, la lezione del giudice Vitelli: "Perché Baudelaire mi ha aiutato ad assolvere Stasi". «Sapete come riuscii a risolvere la famosa telefonata di Alberto Stasi al 118 (quella del “credo che abbiano ucciso una persona”)? Grazie a una poesia di Baudelaire». Così il giudice Stefano Vitelli, noto soprattutto per aver emesso la sentenza di primo grado del delitto di Garlasco, racconta agli studenti del liceo Umberto Eco di Alessandria come ha affrontato una delle decisioni più importanti della sua vita: quella che il 17 dicembre 2009 portò all’assoluzione di Alberto Stasi dall’accusa di aver ucciso Chiara Poggi. C’è un elemento che il giudice Vitelli non manca di rimarcare a ogni passaggio del suo racconto: il ragionevole dubbio (diventato anche il titolo del libro autobiografico scritto insieme al giornalista de La Stampa, Giuseppe Legato). Perché è proprio il dubitare dell’evidenza che lo ha portato all’assoluzione: «Questo è un caso caratterizzato da continue sorprese - ha spiegato agli studenti -.
